  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The helper does not inspect, hide, or reject `remote.origin.pushurl` and `url.<base>.pushInsteadOf` settings.
  WHY: These settings can retain credentials during the editor run or direct subsequent Git operations to an unvetted destination; severity was MAJOR for google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, and openai_gpt-6-luna, and BLOCKER for z-ai_glm-5_2.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh:lines 45-53, 85-95 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: A generic host-wide `http.https://github.com/.extraheader` is restored under the same generic key instead of being scoped to the verified repository URL.
  WHY: The restored authorization header can apply to GitHub requests beyond the intended checkout, and the cited tests expect only a repository-scoped header.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh:line 56 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Restore exits successfully and silently when its marker is missing or empty.
  WHY: The cited contract test requires a `marker_missing` diagnostic, and the silent exit obscures that hide may not have run.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh:lines 20-28, 57-60, 96-104 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Credential hide and restore failure paths can return success, including when a marker already exists or cannot be created, GH_TOKEN is missing, or a restore operation fails.
  WHY: Callers rely on non-zero status to stop execution, so returning success can allow the editor to run with credentials exposed or conceal failed restoration; the reviewers agree this is a blocker.
- scripts/review_untrusted_workspace.py:line 38 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash]
  PROBLEM: The review autofix transfer filter excludes paths containing the substring `credential`, preventing edits to `scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh` from being transferred back.
  WHY: Review autofix cannot transfer fixes to the vulnerable helper, leaving it unchanged across autofix iterations.

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_8-flash ===
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh:lines 81-85 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The restore action injects GH_TOKEN into any remote origin URL matching ^https://github\.com/ without validating that the repository matches the expected repository identity (GITHUB_REPOSITORY or trusted support checkout).
  WHY: An untrusted editor in a heal-evidence run can redirect git origin to an external repository on github.com (e.g. https://github.com/attacker/repo.git). When scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh restore runs, it approves the origin because it starts with https://github.com/ and injects GH_TOKEN, causing subsequent git fetch or push steps in implement.yml to exfiltrate the token to the attacker's repository. In addition, test_restore_does_not_send_token_to_an_editor_changed_origin in tests/test_heal_evidence_editor_isolation.py:64-67 asserts that restoring an editor-changed origin fails with a non-zero exit code and does not write the secret into config, which fails at runtime.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh:lines 35-53, 78-95 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The helper only inspects and hides remote.origin.url, ignoring remote.origin.pushurl and url.<base>.pushInsteadOf.
  WHY: An untrusted editor can configure remote.origin.pushurl or url.<base>.pushInsteadOf rewrites pointing to an external destination. Neither hide nor restore validates or clears these settings, so subsequent git push steps in implement.yml will target the unvetted push destination. Furthermore, test_hide_rejects_an_explicit_push_url_before_editor_launch, test_restore_rejects_editor_changed_push_url, and test_restore_rejects_editor_changed_push_url_rewrite in tests/test_heal_evidence_editor_isolation.py assert rejection of these configurations and fail at runtime.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh:lines 87-95 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Generic extraheader configuration http.https://github.com/.extraheader is restored verbatim rather than scoped to the specific repository URL.
  WHY: Restoring http.https://github.com/.extraheader applies the AUTHORIZATION: basic <token> header to all github.com requests across any repository or host rather than scoping it to http.https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>.git.extraheader. Furthermore, tests/test_heal_evidence_editor_isolation.py:42-43 asserts that the generic extraheader is not set and that only the repository-scoped extraheader is set, failing at runtime.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh:line 56 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: When restore is invoked without an existing or non-empty marker, the script exits immediately with exit 0 without writing any diagnostic output.
  WHY: tests/test_heal_evidence_editor_isolation.py:28-30 executes editor_git_credentials.sh restore before hide and asserts that stderr contains reason=marker_missing. Because line 56 silently exits 0 without diagnostic output, the test fails at runtime.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh:lines 20-28, 57-60, 96-104 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The script fails open by returning exit code 0 on hide and restore failures.
  WHY: Callers run editor_git_credentials.sh under set -e expecting failures to stop execution. Exiting 0 on failure masks failures to hide credentials (leaving the editor with active credentials) and failures to restore credentials. Line 24 and line 28 exit 0 on hide errors, line 59 exits 0 when GH_TOKEN is unset on restore, and line 104 unconditionally executes exit 0 even when failed=true was set during restore. Additionally, tests in tests/test_heal_evidence_editor_isolation.py assert that restore exits non-zero on error, causing test failures.
- scripts/review_untrusted_workspace.py:line 38 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The review autofix transfer filter excludes any path containing the substring credential, preventing changes to scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh from being transferred back from the review isolation container.
  WHY: Review autofix executes the editor in an isolated container and transfers modified files back using review_untrusted_workspace.py from the verified workflow support commit on main. Because main excludes *credential* and does not yet contain this PR's scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh exemption, any fix to scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh made by the review editor is rejected at transfer time, leaving the committed file stuck at its vulnerable 102-line baseline across autofix iterations. Renaming the helper to avoid credential (e.g. scripts/editor_git_auth.sh) or staging support updates is necessary to allow review autofix to maintain the script.
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_8-flash ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh:lines 81-83, `if [[ "${url}" =~ ^https://github\.com/ ]]; then repo_git "${repo}" remote set-url origin "https://x-access-token:${GH_TOKEN}@${url#https://}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || failed=true` | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The restore action injects GH_TOKEN into any `https://github.com/` origin without checking that the origin points at the expected repository (GITHUB_REPOSITORY or trusted support checkout).
  WHY: An untrusted editor that runs in a heal-evidence session can change the checkout's `remote.origin.url` to `https://github.com/attacker/repo.git`. The restore predicate matches `^https://github\.com/`, so it writes the token into the attacker's URL; subsequent `git push` / `git fetch` steps in `implement.yml` exfiltrate GH_TOKEN. The test `tests/test_heal_evidence_editor_isolation.py:55-73` (`test_restore_does_not_send_token_to_an_editor_changed_origin`) sets up exactly this scenario and asserts that the script returns non-zero and that `newsecret` never lands in `.git/config`. With the current implementation, both assertions fail: the non-github.com case exits 0 (line 102 unconditional `exit 0`) and the github.com attacker case writes the token before exiting 0.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh:lines 35-53 (hide loop) and 78-95 (restore loop) | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The helper only inspects `remote.origin.url` and `http.*.extraheader`. It never reads `remote.origin.pushurl` or any `url.<base>.pushInsteadOf` rewrite, so the hide does not strip them and the restore does not reject an editor-changed value.
  WHY: After hide, an editor (or a misconfigured CI step that reuses the workspace) can set `remote.origin.pushurl=https://github.com/attacker/repo.git` or add `url.https://github.com/attacker/repo.git.pushInsteadOf=https://github.com/owner/repo.git`. The next credentialed `git push` (or, post-restore, any fetch) targets the attacker URL, and the `tests/test_heal_evidence_editor_isolation.py` cases `test_hide_rejects_an_explicit_push_url_before_editor_launch`, `test_restore_rejects_editor_changed_push_url`, `test_restore_rejects_editor_changed_push_url_rewrite` (all in the `test_heal_evidence_editor_isolation.py` block at lines 95-225 of the original PR) explicitly require rejection, which the current code does not provide.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh:lines 45-53 (hide extraheader capture) and 85-93 (restore extraheader writeback) | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Hide captures the exact extraheader key it found and the restore writes the new credential back to that same key. The capture regex `^http\..*\.extraheader$` matches both generic keys (`http.https://github.com/.extraheader`) and per-repo keys (`http.https://github.com/owner/repo.extraheader`); there is no scoping step that rewrites a generic key into the verified origin's key.
